entry.summary: Will Port St. Lucie see more floods this weekend?    WPEC
entry.article_text: This weekend we're expected to see more heavy rain in our area. This may be exactly the kind of weekend forecast that many people in Port St. Lucie do not want to hear. Last week, parts of the city flooded when torrential rains hit Port St. According to our Stormtrac meteorologists, the city got about four inches of rain in a 48 hour period last week. Roads turned into lakes, water levels in canals rose quickly, and some drivers took their chances and drove through standing water deep enough to possibly leave them stalled with nowhere to go. One homeowner, who has a canal directly behind his house, says the flooding was unlike anything he had ever seen in the two years he's lived in Port St. See also: Trump expected at Mar-a-Lago as Palm Beach road closures, No Kings rallies are planned "When I came out, I was like, Oh, my God. I've never seen it like this before!" said Peter Rodriguez, who lives at the intersection of SW Todd Avenue and SW Broadview Street in Port St. How concerned is he about the possibility of another flood this weekend? "I don't think it's gonna get that high. If it starts getting that high, then I'm gonna start to pray. Not another flood," he said. A city spokesman says they'll have public works employees on standby this weekend if heavy rain comes, and they need to clear storm drains or move pumps into position to lower water levels in certain areas such as near the intersection of Savona Boulevard California Boulevard.

entry.title: Amendment 3 could bring rush of Florida homebuyers, impact property values
entry.summary: Amendment 3 aims to change the property tax structure in Florida by saving money for homeowners and cutting revenue for cities and counties. It could have an impact on the Florida real estate market. A 2025 study by Realtor.com suggests home values in Florida could rise 7% to 9% if the referendum passes, and some real estate professionals say there will likely be an impact. WATCH BELOW: Amendment 3 could shake up Florida housing market Amendment 3 and Real Estate 'I don't see them going up to like the 7, 8, 9, 10 percent,' says Jeff Lichtenstein of Echo Fine Properties in Palm Beach Gardens. However, he does see a possible rush of buyers entering the market. 'You better be prepared because if it happens, it will happen fast,' Lichtenstein said. 'I think there will be a mad rush to get in here, because if not, then you're waiting five years.' That's because the referendum requires homeowners to be homesteaded in Florida by Dec 31 to receive the full tax savings right away. New home buyers entering the state would have a five-year waiting period to get the full homestead exemption. The Florida Realtors is publicly supporting Amendment 3 but isn't convinced about property values rising quickly. 'The cost of home is economically driven,' Florida Realtors CEO Margy Grant. 'It's a supply and demand conversation, and when inventory increases, prices stabilize and we've seen that in recent months.' Amendment 3 needs 60% of the vote to pass on November 3.

entry.title: 33 years after uncle's murder, family asks Gov. Ron DeSantis to sign killer's death warrant
entry.summary: Thirty-three years after his uncle was murdered, Brian Kunkel is still waiting for what he considers justice. 'There's a whole host of emotions with this,' Kunkel said. 'There's a tremendous amount of anger, and now as we speak, it kind of starts to build back up again.' WATCH BELOW: 'It's time': Family seeks execution 33 years after loved one murdered Family seeks execution 33 years after man killed in West Palm Beach His uncle, Richard Kunkel, was a 32-year-old local florist remembered by his family as outgoing, generous and full of life. 'Richard was a fun-loving guy,' Brian Kunkel said. 'He had a great spirit. Very friendly. Very outgoing the type of person that literally would give you the shirt off his back.' In 1993, Richard Kunkel went to Roosters nightclub in West Palm Beach. Court records show Ronald Knight and two other men went to the gay bar looking for a man to lure away, rob and beat. 'This was all premeditated,' Brian Kunkel said. 'He knew what he was doing.' Court records show the men befriended Kunkel and convinced him to leave with them. Knight then drove him to a secluded area, where he shot and killed him. The men robbed Kunkel, stole his car and burglarized his home. 'Richard begged for his life,' Brian Kunkel said. 'He pleaded not to be shot. He was murdered in cold blood.' Two years later, Knight was charged in another killing. In May 1995, 22-year-old Brendan Meehan was lured from Heartbreakers, then a gay nightclub on Olive Avenue in West Palm Beach, taken to a secluded area and killed. Knight was convicted of both murders and sentenced to death in 1998. 'These people had purposes in life, and it's gone,' Kunkel said. A family waiting for an execution More than three decades after Richard Kunkel's murder, Knight remains on death row. Now, Kunkel is asking Gov. Ron DeSantis to sign his death warrant. 'It's been a long and arduous process,' he said. 'My grandparents are gone. They've passed without closure, and I know, at least in my grandmother's case, she died of really a broken heart.' 'This needs to be done. It needs to be finalized,' Kunkel added. His request comes as Florida carries out executions at a pace rarely seen in the state. Florida executed a record 19 people in 2025. Seventeen people have been executed so far in 2026, with two more executions scheduled. That pace has drawn concern from death penalty opponents and defense attorneys, who warn increasingly compressed timelines could put additional strain on the appeals

entry.title: Port St. Lucie tests new water sensors as weekend rain threatens flood-prone areas
entry.summary: More rain is expected this weekend across South Florida and the Treasure Coast, and WPTV is learning that Port St. Lucie Public Works is preparing. Scott Samples, communications manager with the City of Port St. Lucie, said crews spent the week clearing debris from drains and grates. WATCH BELOW: Port St. Lucie prepares for rain, flooding concerns Port St. Lucie prepares for rain, flooding concerns Samples added that water levels in retention ponds and canals are at an adequate level and won't need to be lowered. Staff have also been testing their new pilot water sensors, which will send alerts to select staff if water levels rise. 'It's a way for us to respond faster to very specific locations,' Samples said. Jennifer Collins, owner of Pets Play Grooming off California and Savona boulevards, said her staff is preparing too. 'We're nervous about this storm coming up this week,' Collins said. 'Every time it rains, we get scared.' Collins is no stranger to flooding on California and Savona boulevards. She said flooding has occurred there for years. WPTV was there when water levels rose at the intersection last week. Collins said she already sent messages to her customers for Saturday. 'We may have to reschedule their dogs. We may have to push them off to next week,' Collins said. 'Saturdays are one of our busiest days, so it does really affect us as a small business.' For long-term solutions at the intersection, the city is working on a large-scale drainage project for the Oak Hammock neighborhood, which includes raising portions of the roadway. 'When this project is completed, those problems won't be problems anymore,' Samples said. The drainage project is still in data collection before moving on to design. 'We can't work if it's raining, and that's in Florida,' Collins said. 'That's just not OK.' The project may take years until completion, but Collins said she already thought about moving her business. 'We've also talked about possibly moving, and you know that would be hard too,' Collins said. 'I just feel like it's not, not getting better.'

entry.title: 'He just tried to ram me': Port St. Lucie man arrested after a chase ends on South Hutchinson Island - WPBF
entry.summary: 'He just tried to ram me': Port St. Lucie man arrested after a chase ends on South Hutchinson Island    WPBF
entry.article_text: Lucie man was arrested Thursday night after leading St. Lucie County deputies on a high-speed chase that ended on South Hutchinson Island. The pursuit began in the 9600 block of South Ocean Boulevard when a Patrol Operations deputy attempted to stop the driver of a pickup truck for a traffic violation. Andrew Bolonka, the director of communications for the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, said the driver fled instead of stopping, making a U-turn and spinning donuts in the roadway, forcing other motorists to take evasive action. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates After briefly stopping, the driver made another U-turn, cut across lanes of traffic, and accelerated toward the deputy's patrol vehicle. "The deputy tries to stop the vehicle; all of a sudden, the vehicle lunges, takes off, accelerates, does another U-turn, and then starts allegedly heading straight toward the deputy. Which you can see in the body-worn camera, where the deputy makes an evasive maneuver and says, 'Oh, he almost hit me,'" Bolonka said. Members of the department's Special Investigations Unit and deputies in the air assisted in the pursuit. The driver continued to flee even after stop sticks were deployed. Deputies eventually executed a PIT maneuver along Seaway Drive, bringing the vehicle to a stop. Despite repeated verbal commands to exit the truck, the driver refused, prompting deputies to deploy pepper balls into the vehicle. The driver then surrendered and was taken into custody without further incident. The suspect, identified as 37-year-old Joshua Gallagher of Port St. Lucie, faces several charges, including aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, possession of a controlled substance without a prescription, and resisting arrest without violence. He remains in custody at the St. "When people make decisions like this, and they commit an act that puts not only the deputies and other law enforcement officers in peril, but they are also putting the general public in peril. If we can do so safely, we're going to put it to an end," Bolonka said. Authorities expressed relief that no one was injured during the incident. entry.title: Palm Beach seawall replacement will close popular beach for 18 months
entry.summary: Behind the peach paint and scalloped edges of a familiar Palm Beach seawall is a structure that engineers say has reached the end of its useful life after more than a century of protecting the island. Now, the town is preparing for a major replacement project that will change the look of the beachfront and close the beach for about a year and a half. WATCH BELOW: Seawall replacement will close this beach for 18 months Palm Beach seawall replacement to close beach for 18 months The pastel-colored seawall has long blended into the scenery along a beach frequented by tourists and locals. Sandra Greenberg, who was visiting with her family from Virginia and has a condo in West Palm Beach, described it simply: 'It's a great beach, love it.' A tourist visiting from Costa Rica shared the sentiment, saying, 'Yes, it's perfect.' For people who live nearby, however, the beach can be more than a destination. It is part of their regular routine. 'This is where I come to, like, relax,' said Bridget St. Laurent, a local and owner of Palm Beach Beauty Lab on Palm Beach. 'It's my life, it's my backyard, I grew up here, and the fact I can just take a five-minute drive to the ocean means so much.' St. Laurent told WPTV she tries to visit once a week, if not more. But that routine is about to be interrupted. The seawall is one line of defense from hurricanes and storm surges that, over more than a century, has protected the island from what is estimated to be $7 billion in private property, along with critical infrastructure on Palm Beach. Replacing it will require a lengthy beach closure, with the project expected to keep beachgoers away for approximately a year and a half. 'A year and a half? That's so sad,' St. Laurent said after learning from WPTV how long the closure would last. For regular visitors, the project means they will have to find another stretch of sand until the work is complete. Other beach options include Singer Island to the north, as well as Phipps Beach and Lake Worth Beach to the south. entry.article_text: Behind the peach paint and scalloped edges of a familiar Palm Beach seawall is a structure that engineers say has reached the end of its useful life after more than a century of protecting the island.Now, the town is preparing for a major replacement project that will change the look of the beachfront and close the beach for about a year and a half.WATCH BELOW: Seawall replacement will close this beach for 18 monthsThe pastel-colored seawall has long blended into the scenery along a beach frequented by tourists and locals. Sandra Greenberg, who was visiting with her family from Virginia and has a condo in West Palm Beach, described it simply: "It's a great beach, love it."A tourist visiting from Costa Rica shared the sentiment, saying, "Yes, it's perfect."For people who live nearby, however, the beach can be more than a destination. It is part of their regular routine."This is where I come to, like, relax," said Bridget St. Laurent, a local and owner of Palm Beach Beauty Lab on Palm Beach. "It's my life, it's my backyard, I grew up here, and the fact I can just take a five-minute drive to the ocean means so much."St. Laurent told WPTV she tries to visit once a week, if not more.But that routine is about to be interrupted.The seawall is one line of defense from hurricanes and storm surges that, over more than a century, has protected the island from what is estimated to be $7 billion in private property, along with critical infrastructure on Palm Beach.Replacing it will require a lengthy beach closure, with the project expected to keep beachgoers away for approximately a year and a half."A year and a half? Laurent said after learning from WPTV how long the closure would last.For regular visitors, the project means they will have to find another stretch of sand until the work is complete. Other beach options include Singer Island to the north, as well as Phipps Beach and Lake Worth Beach to the south.When WPTV reporter Joel Lopez asked Greenberg where she might go during the closure, she didn't have an alternative in mind."No, you're going to have to tell me where to go," she said.Still, Greenberg said she understands why the work needs to be done, even if that means temporarily losing access to a beach her family enjoys."We're going to have to do it; let's just rip that band-aid off and get it done," Greenberg said.The preparations are expected to become visible by the end of the year, when the pastel backdrop will be covered by fencing as work gets underway on the next chapter of the seawall."It's going to be a little bit of a nuisance for now, but more importantly we need to keep this community safe," Greenberg said.For St. Laurent, the construction may keep her away for a while, but it won't keep her away permanently.Asked whether she would return once the year-and-a-half project is finished, St. Laurent said, "Absolutely, I live here; this is my backyard."A wildlife deterrent will also be created, including a turtle berm, a small wall to protect sea turtles from clashing with the construction.Engineers say the new seawall will also include the iconic scalloped border.Before construction gets underway, the town is also giving the community an opportunity to learn more about what is planned. entry.title: Will Port St. Lucie see more floods this weekend? - cw34.com
entry.summary: Will Port St. Lucie see more floods this weekend?    cw34.com
entry.article_text: This weekend we're expected to see more heavy rain in our area. This may be exactly the kind of weekend forecast that many people in Port St. Lucie do not want to hear. Last week, parts of the city flooded when torrential rains hit Port St. According to our Stormtrac meteorologists, the city got about four inches of rain in a 48 hour period last week. Roads turned into lakes, water levels in canals rose quickly, and some drivers took their chances and drove through standing water deep enough to possibly leave them stalled with nowhere to go. One homeowner, who has a canal directly behind his house, says he was stunned to see the extent of the flooding. It was the worst he's seen in the two years he's lived in Port St. See also: Trump expected at Mar-a-Lago as Palm Beach road closures, No Kings rallies are planned "When I came out, I was like, Oh, my God! I've never seen it like this before!" said Peter Rodriguez, who lives at the intersection of SW Todd Avenue and SW Broadview Street in Port St. How concerned is he about the possibility of another flood this weekend? "I don't think it's gonna get that high. If it starts getting that high, then I'm gonna start to pray. Not another flood," he said. Luckily floodwater did not get into his house. But the water was deep enough he says, to prevent him from driving out of his driveway. One resident says he feels the city of Port St. Lucie could be doing more to prevent such flooding. "I really think they should do something, I mean really to take care of business, you know because we pay our taxes," said Frank Camarda, a Port St. Lucie resident on SW Leisure Lane. A city spokesman says they'll have Public Works employees on standby this weekend if heavy rain comes, if they need to clear storm drains or move pumps into position to lower water levels in certain areas such as near the intersection of Savona Boulevard and SW California Boulevard. That area has been prone to flooding in the past. "They've been monitoring the canals and the retention ponds. And again, they haven't had to lower them this week which is a good sign. They're where they think they need to be. So, we're as prepared as we can be. You never know what Mother Nature is going to throw at you, but this team is doing everything it can to try to to mitigate the risks as much as possible," said Scott Samples, Strategic Communications Manager and Public Information Officer, city of Port St. He says the city of Port St. Lucie received no reports last week that floodwaters got into any homes or businesses.

entry.title: 'He just tried to ram me': Port St. Lucie man arrested after a chase ends on South Hutchinson Island - WPBF
entry.summary: 'He just tried to ram me': Port St. Lucie man arrested after a chase ends on South Hutchinson Island    WPBF
entry.article_text: Lucie man was arrested Thursday night after leading St. Lucie County deputies on a high-speed chase that ended on South Hutchinson Island. The pursuit began in the 9600 block of South Ocean Boulevard when a Patrol Operations deputy attempted to stop the driver of a pickup truck for a traffic violation. Andrew Bolonka, the director of communications for the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, said the driver fled instead of stopping, making a U-turn and spinning donuts in the roadway, forcing other motorists to take evasive action. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates After briefly stopping, the driver made another U-turn, cut across lanes of traffic, and accelerated toward the deputy's patrol vehicle. "The deputy tries to stop the vehicle; all of a sudden, the vehicle lunges, takes off, accelerates, does another U-turn, and then starts allegedly heading straight toward the deputy. Which you can see in the body-worn camera, where the deputy makes an evasive maneuver and says, 'Oh, he almost hit me,'" Bolonka said. Members of the department's Special Investigations Unit and deputies in the air assisted in the pursuit. The driver continued to flee even after stop sticks were deployed. Deputies eventually executed a PIT maneuver along Seaway Drive, bringing the vehicle to a stop. Despite repeated verbal commands to exit the truck, the driver refused, prompting deputies to deploy pepper balls into the vehicle. The driver then surrendered and was taken into custody without further incident. The suspect, identified as 37-year-old Joshua Gallagher of Port St. Lucie, faces several charges, including aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, possession of a controlled substance without a prescription, and resisting arrest without violence. He remains in custody at the St. "When people make decisions like this, and they commit an act that puts not only the deputies and other law enforcement officers in peril, but they are also putting the general public in peril. If we can do so safely, we're going to put it to an end," Bolonka said. Authorities expressed relief that no one was injured during the incident. entry.title: 33 years after uncle's murder, family asks Gov. Ron DeSantis to sign killer's death warrant
entry.summary: Thirty-three years after his uncle was murdered, Brian Kunkel is still waiting for what he considers justice. 'There's a whole host of emotions with this,' Kunkel said. 'There's a tremendous amount of anger, and now as we speak, it kind of starts to build back up again.' WATCH BELOW: 'It's time': Family seeks execution 33 years after loved one murdered Family seeks execution 33 years after man killed in West Palm Beach His uncle, Richard Kunkel, was a 32-year-old local florist remembered by his family as outgoing, generous and full of life. 'Richard was a fun-loving guy,' Brian Kunkel said. 'He had a great spirit. Very friendly. Very outgoing the type of person that literally would give you the shirt off his back.' In 1993, Richard Kunkel went to Roosters nightclub in West Palm Beach. Court records show Ronald Knight and two other men went to the gay bar looking for a man to lure away, rob and beat. 'This was all premeditated,' Brian Kunkel said. 'He knew what he was doing.' Court records show the men befriended Kunkel and convinced him to leave with them. Knight then drove him to a secluded area, where he shot and killed him. The men robbed Kunkel, stole his car and burglarized his home. 'Richard begged for his life,' Brian Kunkel said. 'He pleaded not to be shot. He was murdered in cold blood.' Two years later, Knight was charged in another killing. In May 1995, 22-year-old Brendan Meehan was lured from Heartbreakers, then a gay nightclub on Olive Avenue in West Palm Beach, taken to a secluded area and killed. Knight was convicted of both murders and sentenced to death in 1998. 'These people had purposes in life, and it's gone,' Kunkel said. A family waiting for an execution More than three decades after Richard Kunkel's murder, Knight remains on death row. Now, Kunkel is asking Gov. Ron DeSantis to sign his death warrant. 'It's been a long and arduous process,' he said. 'My grandparents are gone. They've passed without closure, and I know, at least in my grandmother's case, she died of really a broken heart.' 'This needs to be done. It needs to be finalized,' Kunkel added. His request comes as Florida carries out executions at a pace rarely seen in the state. Florida executed a record 19 people in 2025. Seventeen people have been executed so far in 2026, with two more executions scheduled. That pace has drawn concern from death penalty opponents and defense attorneys, who warn increasingly compressed timelines could put additional strain on the appeals

entry.title: Will Port St. Lucie see more floods this weekend? - WPEC
entry.summary: Will Port St. Lucie see more floods this weekend?    WPEC
entry.article_text: This weekend we're expected to see more heavy rain in our area. This may be exactly the kind of weekend forecast that many people in Port St. Lucie do not want to hear. Last week, parts of the city flooded when torrential rains hit Port St. According to our Stormtrac meteorologists, the city got about four inches of rain in a 48 hour period last week. Roads turned into lakes, water levels in canals rose quickly, and some drivers took their chances and drove through standing water deep enough to possibly leave them stalled with nowhere to go. One homeowner, who has a canal directly behind his house, says he was stunned to see the extent of the flooding. It was the worst he's seen in the two years he's lived in Port St. See also: Trump expected at Mar-a-Lago as Palm Beach road closures, No Kings rallies are planned "When I came out, I was like, Oh, my God! I've never seen it like this before!" said Peter Rodriguez, who lives at the intersection of SW Todd Avenue and SW Broadview Street in Port St. How concerned is he about the possibility of another flood this weekend? "I don't think it's gonna get that high. If it starts getting that high, then I'm gonna start to pray. Not another flood," he said. Luckily floodwater did not get into his house. But the water was deep enough he says, to prevent him from driving out of his driveway. One resident says he feels the city of Port St. Lucie could be doing more to prevent such flooding. "I really think they should do something, I mean really to take care of business, you know because we pay our taxes," said Frank Camarda, a Port St. Lucie resident on SW Leisure Lane. A city spokesman says they'll have Public Works employees on standby this weekend if heavy rain comes, if they need to clear storm drains or move pumps into position to lower water levels in certain areas such as near the intersection of Savona Boulevard and SW California Boulevard. That area has been prone to flooding in the past. "They've been monitoring the canals and the retention ponds. And again, they haven't had to lower them this week which is a good sign. They're where they think they need to be. So, we're as prepared as we can be. You never know what Mother Nature is going to throw at you, but this team is doing everything it can to try to to mitigate the risks as much as possible," said Scott Samples, Strategic Communications Manager and Public Information Officer, city of Port St. He says the city of Port St. Lucie received no reports last week that floodwaters got into any homes or businesses.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie tests new water sensors as weekend rain threatens flood-prone areas - WFLX
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie tests new water sensors as weekend rain threatens flood-prone areas    WFLX
entry.article_text: More rain is expected this weekend across South Florida and the Treasure Coast, and WPTV is learning that Port St. Lucie Public Works is preparing. Scott Samples, communications manager with the City of Port St. Lucie, said crews spent the week clearing debris from drains and grates. Lucie prepares for rain, flooding concerns Samples added that water levels in retention ponds and canals are at an adequate level and won't need to be lowered. Staff have also been testing their new pilot water sensors, which will send alerts to select staff if water levels rise. "It's a way for us to respond faster to very specific locations," Samples said. Jennifer Collins, owner of Pets Play Grooming off California and Savona boulevards, said her staff is preparing too. "We're nervous about this storm coming up this week," Collins said. "Every time it rains, we get scared." Collins is no stranger to flooding on California and Savona boulevards. She said flooding has occurred there for years. WPTV was there when water levels rose at the intersection last week. Collins said she already sent messages to her customers for Saturday. "We may have to reschedule their dogs. We may have to push them off to next week," Collins said. "Saturdays are one of our busiest days, so it does really affect us as a small business." For long-term solutions at the intersection, the city is working on a large-scale drainage project for the Oak Hammock neighborhood, which includes raising portions of the roadway. "When this project is completed, those problems won't be problems anymore," Samples said. The drainage project is still in data collection before moving on to design. "We can't work if it's raining, and that's in Florida," Collins said. "That's just not OK." The project may take years until completion, but Collins said she already thought about moving her business. "We've also talked about possibly moving, and you know that would be hard too," Collins said. "I just feel like it's not, not getting better."

entry.title: Amendment 3 could bring rush of Florida homebuyers, impact property values
entry.summary: Amendment 3 aims to change the property tax structure in Florida by saving money for homeowners and cutting revenue for cities and counties. It could also have an impact on the Florida real estate market. A 2025 study by Realtor.com suggests home values in Florida could rise 7% to 9% if the referendum passes, and some real estate professionals say there will likely be an impact. WATCH BELOW: Amendment 3 could shake up Florida housing market Amendment 3 and Real Estate 'I don't see them going up to like the 7, 8, 9, 10 percent,' says Jeff Lichtenstein of Echo Fine Properties in Palm Beach Gardens. However, he does see a possible rush of buyers entering the market. 'You better be prepared because if it happens, it will happen fast,' Lichtenstein said. 'I think there will be a mad rush to get in here, because if not, then you're waiting five years.' That's because the referendum requires homeowners to be homesteaded in Florida by Dec 31 to receive the full tax savings right away. New home buyers entering the state would have a five-year waiting period to get the full homestead exemption. The Florida Realtors is publicly supporting Amendment 3 but isn't convinced about property values rising quickly. 'The cost of home is economically driven,' Florida Realtors CEO Margy Grant. 'It's a supply and demand conversation, and when inventory increases, prices stabilize and we've seen that in recent months.' Amendment 3 needs 60% of the vote to pass on November 3.

entry.summary: Do you know the difference between a macaroon and a macaron? WPTVs Christy Waite visited the GreenMarket in downtown West Palm Beach, where she learned the difference between the two and caught up with a popular local vendor making its return after a yearlong hiatus. entry.summary: Protesters gathered in Palm Beach County as part of a nationwide No Kings day of action, with local organizers putting a focus on encouraging people to vote early ahead of the November midterm elections. The rally was organized locally by Speaking Up for America - Indivisible. Group leader Susan Foley said Saturdays demonstration marked the organizations eighth rally in two years and its fourth No Kings rally. Today is a special day, our fourth No Kings rally, Foley said. This one is special because of its mission to vote early. WATCH: Palm Beach County No Kings rally urges early voting No Kings Rally Foley said organizers are encouraging people to cast their ballots early rather than waiting until Election Day. If you vote early, your vote is locked in, Foley said. But for protesters who came out Saturday, the rally was also an opportunity to speak about issues they would like to see addressed both nationally and closer to home. WPTV's Christy Waite listened to protesters like Ann Hunter. She says she wants to see more attention paid to the financial challenges facing families. More consideration to the middle class and people that are in desperate circumstances struggling with their food, healthcare, everyday living expenses, Hunter said. For Cynthia Heller, a former educator, education funding is among the issues that brought her out. I was in education, so I would like to see more money go into education, Heller said. Protesters said events like Saturdays also give members of the community an opportunity to come together around issues that are important to them. One protester emphasized that regardless of political affiliation, participating in the election is what matters. I am happy to see people here, and no matter how they vote, they have to vote, the protester said. Similar demonstrations have taken place across the region, from Palm Beach County to Vero Beach, as protesters continue to make their voices heard ahead of the November elections.

entry.title: Man found dead after barricade situation in St. Lucie County, deputies say
entry.summary: A man was found dead from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound Saturday after a barricade situation prompted deputies to evacuate a woman and children from a St. Lucie County home, according to the sheriffs office. The St. Lucie County Sheriffs Office said deputies responded around 10:17 a.m. to a reported domestic violence incident in the 7600 block of Winter Garden Boulevard. Deputies initially encountered a man in the front yard who went back inside after seeing law enforcement. Authorities later made contact with a man and woman at the front door. During that interaction, a deputy saw what appeared to be a firearm in the mans possession and ordered him to drop it, the sheriffs office said. Instead, the man closed the door and retreated inside, creating a barricaded-subject situation while other people remained in the home. According to investigators, the man came outside several times and said he would surrender after making a phone call, but repeatedly went back inside. During his final retreat into the home, deputies heard what appeared to be a gunshot. Knowing an adult woman and children were still inside and could be in danger, deputies entered the residence and evacuated them through a side window, the sheriffs office said. Deputies later found the man dead from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound. Authorities said there is no ongoing threat to the community. Detectives, crime scene technicians and investigators from the Medical Examiners Office are expected to remain at the scene for several hours as the investigation continues.

entry.title: President Trump returns to Palm Beach as midterm elections approach
entry.summary: President Donald Trump returned to Palm Beach on Friday for his first trip of the season to Mar-a-Lago, bringing the heightened security and traffic impacts that accompany presidential visits as the country moves closer to the 2026 midterm elections. Trump arrived in South Florida after campaigning Friday in Dalton, Georgia, where he rallied alongside Republican candidates as the party works to turn out voters ahead of Election Day. WPTV saw supporters lining the route toward Trump's Mar-a-Lago estate as his motorcade traveled through Palm Beach. Among them was the Campbell family, who had traveled from South Carolina for a baseball tournament. 'I wasn't expecting this on my bingo card. I thought we were playing baseball,' one member of the Campbell family told WPTV. 'But I'm glad we get to see this.' Trump pushes Republican voters to turn out Trump's arrival came directly after his campaign stop at Dalton Municipal Airport in Georgia, where he appeared with Republican U.S. Senate candidate Mike Collins and gubernatorial candidate Rick Jackson. The Georgia Senate race has become a significant midterm battleground. Recent polling has shown Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff leading Collins. Trump stressed the importance of turnout during his remarks. 'When I'm not on the ballot, I guess it's a compliment, but people don't show up so much,' Trump said. 'So this is, really, I think the most important midterm election I think we've ever had.' The president also told supporters in Dalton that they should 'pretend I'm on the ballot' as he sought to boost Republican enthusiasm. Security increases around Palm Beach Back in Palm Beach, security was heightened around the island ahead of Trump's arrival. Palm Beach County Sheriff Ric Bradshaw recently told WPTV's Michael Hoffman that the county received an exemption allowing license plate reader cameras to remain on state roads as an additional layer of presidential protection. 'We filed a brief with the Department of Highway Safety up there in Tallahassee that, along with the Secret Service, and says, 'Hey, this is why we can't take them down,' and they granted us that exemption,' Bradshaw said. entry.title: Port St. Lucie tests new water sensors as weekend rain threatens flood-prone areas
entry.summary: More rain is expected this weekend across South Florida and the Treasure Coast, and WPTV is learning that Port St. Lucie Public Works is preparing. Scott Samples, communications manager with the City of Port St. Lucie, said crews spent the week clearing debris from drains and grates. WATCH BELOW: Port St. Lucie prepares for rain, flooding concerns Port St. Lucie prepares for rain, flooding concerns Samples added that water levels in retention ponds and canals are at an adequate level and won't need to be lowered. Staff have also been testing their new pilot water sensors, which will send alerts to select staff if water levels rise. 'It's a way for us to respond faster to very specific locations,' Samples said. Jennifer Collins, owner of Pets Play Grooming off California and Savona boulevards, said her staff is preparing too. 'We're nervous about this storm coming up this week,' Collins said. 'Every time it rains, we get scared.' Collins is no stranger to flooding on California and Savona boulevards. She said flooding has occurred there for years. WPTV was there when water levels rose at the intersection last week. Collins said she already sent messages to her customers for Saturday. 'We may have to reschedule their dogs. We may have to push them off to next week,' Collins said. 'Saturdays are one of our busiest days, so it does really affect us as a small business.' For long-term solutions at the intersection, the city is working on a large-scale drainage project for the Oak Hammock neighborhood, which includes raising portions of the roadway. 'When this project is completed, those problems won't be problems anymore,' Samples said. The drainage project is still in data collection before moving on to design. 'We can't work if it's raining, and that's in Florida,' Collins said. 'That's just not OK.' The project may take years until completion, but Collins said she already thought about moving her business. 'We've also talked about possibly moving, and you know that would be hard too,' Collins said. 'I just feel like it's not, not getting better.'

entry.article_text: A man was found dead from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound after deputies responded to a reported domestic violence incident Saturday morning in Fort Pierce's Lakewood Park neighborhood. Deputies responded around 10:17 a.m. to a home in the 7600 block of Winter Garden Boulevard, where they encountered a man in the front yard. The man went back inside after seeing law enforcement, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office . Deputies say they later contacted a man and woman at the front door. A deputy saw what appeared to be a firearm in the man's possession and ordered him to drop the weapon, but he shut the door and retreated inside, prompting a barricaded-subject situation with other occupants still in the home. See also: Driver tried to ram deputy before PIT maneuver ended chase, SLCSO says During the incident, the man reportedly came outside several times and indicated he would surrender after making a phone call, but repeatedly went back inside, deputies said. During his final retreat into the home, deputies say they heard what appeared to be a gunshot. Concerned for an adult woman and children who remained inside, deputies entered the home without alerting the occupants and evacuated them through a side window, according to the sheriff's office. Deputies later found the man dead from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound. The sheriff's office said there is no ongoing threat to the community. Detectives with the agency's Criminal Investigations Division, crime scene technicians and investigators from the Medical Examiner's Office remained at the scene to investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident. If you or someone you know is struggling with thoughts of suicide, help is available. Call or text 988 to reach the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline , available 24/7. You can also chat at 988lifeline.org

Residents are urged to secure loose outdoor items, use caution on the roads and stay out of rough ocean waters.

entry.title: Jupiter apartment residents raise drainage concerns after heavy rain floods parking areas
entry.summary: Residents at Marino Apartments in Jupiter are raising concerns about drainage after they say heavy rain repeatedly leaves portions of the property covered in standing water, at times forcing families to walk through the water simply to reach their vehicles. Resident James Ortman told WPTV the problem has become part of his family's routine when rain hits. He said the water has risen as high as 10 to 12 inches around the front tires of his truck at its worst. WATCH: Jupiter residents seek answers over apartment flooding Jupiter Residents Seek Answers Over Apartment Flooding | WPTV 'My 9-year-old and 5-year-old should not have to describe to me whether it's a puddle, pond, or lake outside the truck,' Ortman said. WPTV's Samantha Gutierrez has repeatedly reached out to management at Marino Apartments seeking an explanation for the drainage problems and information about what, if anything, will be done to address them. Management had not provided a comment at the time of this report. Family changes routine when water collects For Ortman, the drainage concerns are more than an inconvenience. He said the standing water can affect something as routine as getting his children into the family vehicle. 'If they do, then we may have to go more Crocs, getting them into the truck, and I'll bring their school shoes, their school socks or shoes down,' Ortman said. 'Same thing for me.' Ortman said he does not want his children walking through significant amounts of standing water to reach the vehicle. 'Would you feel comfortable walking your kids through, I don't know, 1,500 square feet of eight inches of water?' he asked. Resident wants lasting solution Ortman said he wants apartment management to understand what residents are experiencing firsthand and address why water continues to collect when heavy rain falls. 'Live through it. Live through it for a few days, and then tell me,' Ortman said. WPTV has not independently verified Ortman's estimates of the water's depth or the size of the affected area. The descriptions of those conditions are based on his account. WPTV also has not received information from Marino Apartments management explaining the cause of the reported drainage problems or whether repairs or other corrective measures are planned. For residents like Ortman, the concern now is what will happen the next time heavy rain arrives and whether conditions will change before then. entry.title: Protesters gather across Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast ahead of midterms - WPBF
entry.summary: Protesters gather across Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast ahead of midterms    WPBF
entry.article_text: Hundreds of residents across the Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast gathered this weekend for "No Kings" protests, urging civic engagement and opposing President Donald Trump’s policies ahead of the midterm elections. Anita Smith, a protester, said, "I am really fed up with the way the institution our government is running." Roger Lyle, another protester, said, "I'm out here to protest the president of the United States because the man is a criminal and he needs to be accounted for." Despite the rain, the protests drew large crowds, with organizers emphasizing the importance of ensuring voters have a plan for the midterms. Just do a little research on what these people have done that want to get into the office, and what do you think they're going to do for you?" Lyle said. Smith added, "Nationwide, it's important because our democracy is turning into fascism and authoritarianism, and we have to correct that." The "No Kings" movement opposes the policies and actions of Trump. On Saturday, protests were planned from the Treasure Coast to southern Palm Beach County. Smith drove from Okeechobee to Port St. Lucie to protest against the current administration and Amendment 3 on property taxes. "Somebody in the fine print is going to get rich off this proposition and nobody is reading the whole thing because it's in legalese and I'm afraid people are going to just vote for it and they don't really know what they're voting for. They think they're going to get money back," Smith said. There were no counterprotesters at the rally. Early voting in the area begins Monday.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie tests new water sensors as weekend rain threatens flood-prone areas - WFLX
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie tests new water sensors as weekend rain threatens flood-prone areas    WFLX
entry.article_text: More rain is expected this weekend across South Florida and the Treasure Coast, and WPTV is learning that Port St. Lucie Public Works is preparing. Scott Samples, communications manager with the City of Port St. Lucie, said crews spent the week clearing debris from drains and grates. Lucie prepares for rain, flooding concerns Samples added that water levels in retention ponds and canals are at an adequate level and won't need to be lowered. Staff have also been testing their new pilot water sensors, which will send alerts to select staff if water levels rise. "It's a way for us to respond faster to very specific locations," Samples said. Jennifer Collins, owner of Pets Play Grooming off California and Savona boulevards, said her staff is preparing too. "We're nervous about this storm coming up this week," Collins said. "Every time it rains, we get scared." Collins is no stranger to flooding on California and Savona boulevards. She said flooding has occurred there for years. WPTV was there when water levels rose at the intersection last week. Collins said she already sent messages to her customers for Saturday. "We may have to reschedule their dogs. We may have to push them off to next week," Collins said. "Saturdays are one of our busiest days, so it does really affect us as a small business." For long-term solutions at the intersection, the city is working on a large-scale drainage project for the Oak Hammock neighborhood, which includes raising portions of the roadway. "When this project is completed, those problems won't be problems anymore," Samples said. The drainage project is still in data collection before moving on to design. "We can't work if it's raining, and that's in Florida," Collins said. "That's just not OK." The project may take years until completion, but Collins said she already thought about moving her business. "We've also talked about possibly moving, and you know that would be hard too," Collins said. "I just feel like it's not, not getting better."

entry.title: No Kings protests bring demonstrators to streets across Palm Beach County, Treasure Coast - WPEC
entry.summary: No Kings protests bring demonstrators to streets across Palm Beach County, Treasure Coast    WPEC
entry.article_text: Signs reading Dump Trump and Trump for Prison rose above a crowd along Palm Beach Lakes Boulevard on Saturday as music played and demonstrators gathered to voice their opposition. Some wore Resist shirts and shirts featuring comedian Stephen Colbert. In a video posted by Palm Beach Indivisibles, a demonstrator sang songs touching on political and social issues into a microphone, drawing a chorus of Free speech chants when a West Palm Beach police officer attempted to stop her. The chanting continued until the officer left. The gathering near Target was one of several No Kings events scheduled across Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast, as Trump returned to Palm Beach for his first visit of the season. For those who came out, the reasons varied, but several protesters interviewed by Palm Beach Indivisibles described a desire for change. See also: President Trump departs Palm Beach for Kentucky rally after Mar-a-Lago RNC fundraiser We don't have enough time to list all the reasons, but mainly we just need to take our country back and make sure that we have love and kindness and compassion in our hearts again, one demonstrator said. Another said they were there to oust Trump. A different attendee joked that former President Barack Obama had called and asked him to show up. Saturday’s demonstrations were part of a nationwide No Kings: Vote Early day of action. Organizers said more than 3,000 events were planned across the country, with a focus on encouraging voter participation ahead of the Nov. The effort marks an added focus for the coalition, which has organized demonstrations against what it describes as an expansion of presidential power. This time, organizers are also encouraging people to check their voter registration, learn about their voting options and make a plan to cast a ballot. They describe the voter outreach as nonpartisan. Where No Kings events were scheduled locally Palm Beach County Palm Beach Gardens: 10 a.m. to noon at PGA Boulevard and Campus Drive. on Palm Beach Lakes Boulevard, east of I-95, between Executive Center Drive and Congress Avenue. Wellington: 12:30 to 1:30 p.m. on the public sidewalk in front of the Veterans Memorial. Boynton Beach: 1 to 3 p.m. at Boynton Beach Boulevard and North Congress Avenue. to noon at Boca Raton City Hall. Treasure Coast Sebastian: 10 to 11 a.m. The address was private, with details available through registration. 1 and Kanner Highway/Colorado Avenue. at the MidFlorida Event Center. Protests coincide with Trump's Palm Beach visit President Trump arrived at Donald J. Trump International Airport shortly after 8 p.m. Friday after a rally in Dalton, Georgia. He left Saturday morning for a rally in Kentucky. His visit brought additional security measures and traffic impacts to Palm Beach. South Ocean Boulevard was closed between South County Road and Southern Boulevard, according to the Town of Palm Beach, which advised drivers heading to the island to use the middle or north bridge. The demonstrations came just days before Palm Beach County’s early voting period begins Oct. Voting is scheduled to continue through Nov. 1, ahead of Election Day on Nov.

entry.title: Bomb threat prompts heavy law enforcement response near Trump airport in West Palm Beach
entry.summary: A bomb threat near Donald J. Trump International Airport prompted a significant law enforcement response Sunday afternoon as President Donald Trump returned to Palm Beach, according to the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office. Authorities said no explosives or suspicious items were found, and airport officials confirmed operations have since returned to normal. The incident unfolded during a busy weekend of presidential travel and heightened security across Palm Beach County. Motorcades, road closures and an increased law enforcement presence were visible throughout the area as Trump traveled to Mar-a-Lago ahead of the midterm elections. Bomb threat near Trump airport prompts major law enforcement response Airport operations return to normal The Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office said deputies responded after receiving information about a bomb threat near the airport. Following an investigation, officials determined there was no active threat. Airport officials said normal operations resumed after the response concluded. The incident comes months after Palm Beach International Airport was renamed Donald J. Trump International Airport. WPTV has previously reported on security concerns and threats involving the airport since the name change, although authorities have not identified any connection between Sundays threat and the airports new name. Residents said major roadways including Belvedere Road, Southern Boulevard and surrounding routes can experience lengthy traffic delays. entry.title: Man dies by suicide after barricaded-subject SWAT situation in Fort Pierce - WPEC
entry.summary: Man dies by suicide after barricaded-subject SWAT situation in Fort Pierce    WPEC
entry.article_text: A man was found dead from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound after deputies responded to a reported domestic violence incident Saturday morning in Fort Pierce's Lakewood Park neighborhood. Deputies responded around 10:17 a.m. to a home in the 7600 block of Winter Garden Boulevard, where they encountered a man in the front yard. The man went back inside after seeing law enforcement, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office . Deputies say they later contacted a man and woman at the front door. A deputy saw what appeared to be a firearm in the man's possession and ordered him to drop the weapon, but he shut the door and retreated inside, prompting a barricaded-subject situation with other occupants still in the home. See also: Driver tried to ram deputy before PIT maneuver ended chase, SLCSO says During the incident, the man reportedly came outside several times and indicated he would surrender after making a phone call, but repeatedly went back inside, deputies said. During his final retreat into the home, deputies say they heard what appeared to be a gunshot. Concerned for an adult woman and children who remained inside, deputies entered the home without alerting the occupants and evacuated them through a side window, according to the sheriff's office. Deputies later found the man dead from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound. The sheriff's office said there is no ongoing threat to the community. Detectives with the agency's Criminal Investigations Division, crime scene technicians and investigators from the Medical Examiner's Office remained at the scene to investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident. If you or someone you know is struggling with thoughts of suicide, help is available. Call or text 988 to reach the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline , available 24/7. You can also chat at 988lifeline.org

entry.summary: WEST PALM BEACH Oxbridge Academy is unveiling its first-ever baseball field, built with a $1.8 million anonymous donation that transformed an empty space into a full ballpark right next to the school. WPTV News got an exclusive first look at the new facility, which features fresh-cut grass, new dirt, fencing, bases, a scoreboard and shady dugouts. The new facilities kick off a new era of baseball for the Thunderwolves. The field is a significant upgrade for a team that previously had to leave campus to practice. Senior Carlo Vasquez plays third base, first base and has also pitched for the team. 'I think it's gonna be good, because we have the field coming. We have a lot of freshmen coming in, so it's gonna be a young program, but for the future, it's gonna be good for them, Vasquez said. Vasquez said the move will benefit the program for years to come. 'We used to go drive to Dyer Park and that was where we practiced at. So it was a lot harder, but we made it work. We used to practice on the soccer field, Vasquez said. Now, instead of commuting, the Thunderwolves will take the field right next to their school. 'It's going to be great. It's going to be a lot easier. It's going to be easier to get the work in, Vasquez said. Leading the program is head coach Juan Bustabad, who brings more than 30 years of professional baseball experience to Oxbridge. Bustabad was the school's first baseball coach until 2016; he returns this year excited to coach on the new field. 'We've been waiting for a long time, and it's finally here and these players are going to enjoy it the whole season, Bustabad said. entry.title: Protesters gather across Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast ahead of midterms - WPBF
entry.summary: Protesters gather across Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast ahead of midterms    WPBF
entry.article_text: Hundreds of residents across the Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast gathered this weekend for "No Kings" protests, urging civic engagement and opposing President Donald Trump’s policies ahead of the midterm elections. Anita Smith, a protester, said, "I am really fed up with the way the institution our government is running." Roger Lyle, another protester, said, "I'm out here to protest the president of the United States because the man is a criminal and he needs to be accounted for." Despite the rain, the protests drew large crowds, with organizers emphasizing the importance of ensuring voters have a plan for the midterms. Just do a little research on what these people have done that want to get into the office, and what do you think they're going to do for you?" Lyle said. Smith added, "Nationwide, it's important because our democracy is turning into fascism and authoritarianism, and we have to correct that." The "No Kings" movement opposes the policies and actions of Trump. On Saturday, protests were planned from the Treasure Coast to southern Palm Beach County. Smith drove from Okeechobee to Port St. Lucie to protest against the current administration and Amendment 3 on property taxes. "Somebody in the fine print is going to get rich off this proposition and nobody is reading the whole thing because it's in legalese and I'm afraid people are going to just vote for it and they don't really know what they're voting for. They think they're going to get money back," Smith said. There were no counterprotesters at the rally. Early voting in the area begins Monday.

entry.title: Bomb threat prompts heavy law enforcement response near Trump airport in Palm Beach County
entry.summary: A bomb threat near Donald J. Trump International Airport prompted a significant law enforcement response Sunday afternoon as President Donald Trump returned to Palm Beach, according to the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office. Authorities said no explosives or suspicious items were found, and airport officials confirmed operations have since returned to normal. Bomb threat near Trump airport prompts major law enforcement response The incident unfolded during a busy weekend of presidential travel and heightened security across Palm Beach County. Motorcades, road closures and an increased law enforcement presence were visible throughout the area as Trump traveled to Mar-a-Lago ahead of the midterm elections. Airport operations return to normal The Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office said deputies responded after receiving information about a bomb threat near the airport. Following an investigation, officials determined there was no active threat. Airport officials said normal operations resumed after the response concluded. The incident comes months after Palm Beach International Airport was renamed Donald J. Trump International Airport. WPTV has previously reported on security concerns and threats involving the airport since the name change, although authorities have not identified any connection between Sundays threat and the airports new name. Neighbors say heavy security is expected Residents who live near the airport said large law enforcement operations and traffic disruptions have become familiar whenever the president visits Palm Beach County. Phil, who lives near the airport, told WPTV drivers often encounter road closures and extensive security measures during presidential visits. 'Any time he's coming in town, traffic is lockdown,' he said. 'We've seen cops, sheriffs, Palm Beach sheriffs all around the whole entire airport.' Residents said major roadways including Belvedere Road, Southern Boulevard and surrounding routes can experience lengthy traffic delays. 'If he's coming through, they'll lock it all down and you're stuck in traffic for at least an hour,' said Phil. Businesses deal with temporary disruptions Business owners along Southern Boulevard told WPTV security operations tied to presidential travel can temporarily affect customers and employees. entry.title: No Kings protests bring demonstrators to streets across Palm Beach County, Treasure Coast - WPEC
entry.summary: No Kings protests bring demonstrators to streets across Palm Beach County, Treasure Coast    WPEC
entry.article_text: Signs reading Dump Trump and Trump for Prison rose above a crowd along Palm Beach Lakes Boulevard on Saturday as music played and demonstrators gathered to voice their opposition. Some wore Resist shirts and shirts featuring comedian Stephen Colbert. In a video posted by Palm Beach Indivisibles, a demonstrator sang songs touching on political and social issues into a microphone, drawing a chorus of Free speech chants when a West Palm Beach police officer attempted to stop her. The chanting continued until the officer left. The gathering near Target was one of several No Kings events scheduled across Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast, as Trump returned to Palm Beach for his first visit of the season. For those who came out, the reasons varied, but several protesters interviewed by Palm Beach Indivisibles described a desire for change. See also: President Trump departs Palm Beach for Kentucky rally after Mar-a-Lago RNC fundraiser We don't have enough time to list all the reasons, but mainly we just need to take our country back and make sure that we have love and kindness and compassion in our hearts again, one demonstrator said. Another said they were there to oust Trump. A different attendee joked that former President Barack Obama had called and asked him to show up. Saturday’s demonstrations were part of a nationwide No Kings: Vote Early day of action. Organizers said more than 3,000 events were planned across the country, with a focus on encouraging voter participation ahead of the Nov. The effort marks an added focus for the coalition, which has organized demonstrations against what it describes as an expansion of presidential power. This time, organizers are also encouraging people to check their voter registration, learn about their voting options and make a plan to cast a ballot. They describe the voter outreach as nonpartisan. Where No Kings events were scheduled locally Palm Beach County Palm Beach Gardens: 10 a.m. to noon at PGA Boulevard and Campus Drive. on Palm Beach Lakes Boulevard, east of I-95, between Executive Center Drive and Congress Avenue. Wellington: 12:30 to 1:30 p.m. on the public sidewalk in front of the Veterans Memorial. Boynton Beach: 1 to 3 p.m. at Boynton Beach Boulevard and North Congress Avenue. to noon at Boca Raton City Hall. Treasure Coast Sebastian: 10 to 11 a.m. The address was private, with details available through registration. 1 and Kanner Highway/Colorado Avenue. at the MidFlorida Event Center. Protests coincide with Trump's Palm Beach visit President Trump arrived at Donald J. Trump International Airport shortly after 8 p.m. Friday after a rally in Dalton, Georgia. He left Saturday morning for a rally in Kentucky. His visit brought additional security measures and traffic impacts to Palm Beach. South Ocean Boulevard was closed between South County Road and Southern Boulevard, according to the Town of Palm Beach, which advised drivers heading to the island to use the middle or north bridge. The demonstrations came just days before Palm Beach County’s early voting period begins Oct. Voting is scheduled to continue through Nov. 1, ahead of Election Day on Nov.

entry.title: Early voting begins in Palm Beach County, Treasure Coast ahead of 2026 general election - WPEC
entry.summary: Early voting begins in Palm Beach County, Treasure Coast ahead of 2026 general election    WPEC
entry.article_text: Early voting begins Monday across Palm Beach County and parts of the Treasure Coast, giving voters an opportunity to cast their ballots ahead of the Nov. The start of early voting comes after a weekend of No Kings protests across South Florida, where organizers encouraged voter participation and urged residents to make a plan to vote early. The demonstrations, held Saturday in communities including West Palm Beach and Palm Beach Gardens, were part of a nationwide movement protesting President Donald Trump and his administration. This weekend’s events placed an additional focus on voter turnout ahead of the 2026 general elections. When and where can you vote early? Early voting schedules vary by county, with some polling locations opening Monday and others later in the week. There are 28 early voting locations. An additional day of early voting is available Nov. to 4 p.m., with extended hours until 6 p.m. Eligible voters can cast their ballots at any designated early voting location within the county where they are registered. Voters should bring a valid photo ID with a signature. Those without acceptable identification may still cast a provisional ballot. In Palm Beach County, voters can check polling location wait times online and use an optional appointment program to schedule their check-in time. Important election deadlines: The deadline to register to vote in the general election was Oct. Voters planning to cast a ballot by mail have until Thursday, Oct. to request that a ballot be mailed to them. Completed vote-by-mail ballots must be received by election officials no later than 7 p.m. In Palm Beach County, ballots returned to a branch office or secure ballot intake station must arrive by 5 p.m. Election Day polling locations will be open from 7 a.m. Find your early voting location: Voters can find polling locations, county-specific hours and additional election information through their local supervisor of elections: Palm Beach County : VotePalmBeach.gov St. Lucie County: StLucieVotes.gov Martin County: MartinVotes.gov Indian River County: VoteIndianRiver.gov Okeechobee County: VoteOkeechobee.gov

entry.summary: Strong winds, dangerous surf hit Treasure Coast, Palm Beaches    WPBF
entry.article_text: Impact weather is creating hazardous conditions across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beaches on Sunday. A wind advisory is in effect for parts of Indian River County, with sustained winds of 20 to 25 miles per hour and gusts up to 40 miles per hour. Wind gusts around 30 miles per hour have already been recorded this Sunday morning from Sebastian and Vero Beach south through Jupiter, West Palm Beach, Boynton Beach and Boca Raton. Meanwhile, a high surf advisory remains in effect along the Atlantic coast, where seas are expected to reach seven to 12 feet. The rough surf is creating dangerous swimming conditions, a high risk of rip currents and the potential for beach erosion. Forecasters are also monitoring an area in the Atlantic with a 30% chance of tropical development over the next seven days, though no immediate impacts to Florida are expected. Residents are urged to secure loose outdoor items, use caution on the roads and stay out of rough ocean waters.

entry.title: Do seatbelts put students at risk in a school bus rollover? An NTSB expert weighs in
entry.summary: A deadly school bus crash in Polk County is raising new questions about how students are protected when a bus rolls over, including whether wearing a seat belt could create an additional danger. WATCH: AN NTSB EXPERT WEIGHS IN ON SCHOOL BUS SEAT BELTS NTSB on school buses seat belt safety Two weeks after the crash, investigative reporter Katie LaGrone put that question directly to Dr. Kristin Poland, a school bus safety expert with the National Transportation Safety Board . The crash killed 16-year-old Adinaluz Prieto Oyola during the morning commute on Oct. 5. According to investigators, the school bus carrying 37 high school students was on its way to Winter Haven High School when another cut slammed into its rear, causing the bus to collide head-on with another vehicle and flip over. Following the crash, Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd was asked whether any of the dozens of students aboard were wearing seat belts at the time of impact. 'Quite frankly, if you try to make everyone put a seat belt on, then we would have had 37 kids hanging from the roof by a seat belt,' Judd said. His comments raise a key safety question: In a rollover crash, do seat belts protect students or potentially put them at greater risk? While Poland said the NTSB cannot yet discuss specifics of its investigation into the Polk County crash, she pointed to what the agency has learned from other school bus crashes. 'The real risk is when theyre violently thrown during the crash sequence about the inside of the bus, where they hit other occupants, or they could potentially hit hard points inside the school bus,' Poland said. According to Poland, properly worn three-point restraints, which include both a lap and shoulder belt, provide the best protection even when a bus overturns. 'Those seat belts are designed so that students can still release the belts even if they're under tension, like if a student is hanging from the belt,' she said. Poland acknowledged that the image of a child hanging by a seat belt after a rollover may sound frightening. But she said the greater danger comes during the crash itself, when an unrestrained student can be thrown around the bus. The NTSB has not determined whether a three-point seat belt could have changed the outcome of the Polk County crash. The school district confirmed the bus involved was only equipped with lap belts as are all the school buses in its fleet, according to a district spokesperson. More than a decade ago, she investigated a St. Lucie County school bus crash that killed 9-year-old Aaron Beauchamp, who was wearing a lap belt at the time.The NTSB investigated that crash and produced simulations demonstrating the difference between the protection provided by a lap belt and the protection provided when a shoulder belt is added.A few years later, the agency formally recommended that school districts in the U.S. upgrade school bus restraints to include both lap and shoulder belts. Florida was among the states called on to make three-point seat belts state law.What does Florida require?Currently, Florida only requires school buses to be equipped with lap belts, but students are not required to wear them.Nearly a decade after the NTSB's recommendation, Poland said some Florida school districts are moving toward three-point lap-and-shoulder belts. “We're seeing some progress with some of the school districts in Florida moving to the passenger lap shoulder belts,” she said.But our investigation found that the majority of public school buses in the state still have lap belts only.Cost is one hurdle. Still, Poland said installing the equipment is only part of improving student safety. "It's not enough just to have the lap shoulder belts on the bus, there also has to be an entire layered approach to ensure that the students are wearing the belts properly," she said. That approach also requires involvement and oversight from school districts and parents, Poland said.But Poland wants to emphasize that school buses remain the safest mode of transportation for students traveling to and from school, regardless of what kind of seat belts are on board. For Poland, seat belt use on school buses is a major step toward the agency's ultimate goal. "We think we can get to zero fatalities in school buses and that's what we're looking towards," Poland said.

entry.title: Ballet Palm Beach brings Mary Shelley's 'Frankenstein' to the Kravis Center in West Palm Beach
entry.summary: Ballet Palm Beach is bringing one of literature's most iconic stories to the stage this month with its original production of Mary Shelley's Frankenstein at the Kravis Center in West Palm Beach. The production runs Oct. 22 through Oct. 24 at the Marshall E. Rinker Sr. Playhouse and reimagines Mary Shelley's classic novel through contemporary ballet. Ballet Palm Beach describes the performance as a dramatic exploration of ambition, abandonment and identity. The company is the professional ballet company of Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast. WATCH BELOW: Ballet Palm Beach brings 'Frankenstein' to the Kravis Center Inside Ballet Palm Beach's world-premiere Frankenstein According to Founding Artistic and Executive Director Colleen Smith, the story begins before Frankenstein's monster ever comes to life. 'It's a gorgeous production about Mary Shelley and her haunting book Frankenstein,' Smith said. During the broadcast, Smith explained how the famous story was born during a gathering at Lake Geneva. 'They were gathered together on the shores of Lake Geneva on a stormy night, and Lord Byron was reading ghost stories and said, 'You know what, guys, let's create our own ghost stories,' and she did,' Smith said. 'First science fiction novel ever written by an 18-year-old woman.' Dancer Leah Walker said audiences can expect something different from a traditional ballet. 'Most classical ballets are fantasy, but ours does follow the real story of Mary Shelley and her process as she writes it,' Leah said. 'It's a horror. It's a very contemporary, very artistic take.' The production is recommended for ages 9 and older and features two 45-minute acts separated by a 20-minute intermission. For audiences looking for a Halloween-season experience with a local arts connection, the performance offers a fresh take on a familiar tale. The production combines historical elements from Mary Shelley's life with the themes that have made Frankenstein one of the most enduring stories ever written. Tickets and performance information are available through Ballet Palm Beach and the Kravis Center. entry.title: Palm Beach County 'No Kings' rally urges early voting
entry.summary: Protesters gathered in Palm Beach County as part of a nationwide 'No Kings' day of action, with local organizers putting a focus on encouraging people to vote early ahead of the November midterm elections. The rally was organized locally by Speaking Up for America - Indivisible. Group leader Susan Foley said Saturday's demonstration marked the organization's eighth rally in two years and its fourth No Kings rally. 'Today is a special day, our fourth No Kings rally,' Foley said. 'This one is special because of its mission to vote early.' WATCH: Palm Beach County No Kings' rally urges early voting No Kings Rally Foley said organizers are encouraging people to cast their ballots early rather than waiting until Election Day. 'If you vote early, your vote is locked in,' Foley said. WPTV's Christy Waite listened to protesters like Ann Hunter. She says she wants to see more attention paid to the financial challenges facing families. 'More consideration to the middle class and people that are in desperate circumstances struggling with their food, healthcare, everyday living expenses,' Hunter said. Protesters said events like Saturday's also give members of the community an opportunity to come together around issues that are important to them. entry.title: Man found dead after barricade situation in St. Lucie County, deputies say
entry.summary: A man was found dead from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound Saturday after a barricade situation prompted deputies to evacuate a woman and children from a St. Lucie County home, according to the sheriffs office. The St. Lucie County Sheriffs Office said deputies responded around 10:17 a.m. to a reported domestic violence incident in the 7600 block of Winter Garden Boulevard. WATCH BELOW: Man found dead after St. Lucie County barricade situation Man found dead after barricade situation in St. Lucie County Deputies initially encountered a man in the front yard who went back inside after seeing law enforcement. Authorities later made contact with a man and woman at the front door. During that interaction, a deputy saw what appeared to be a firearm in the man's possession and ordered him to drop it, the sheriffs office said. Instead, the man closed the door and retreated inside, creating a barricaded-subject situation while other people remained in the home. According to investigators, the man came outside several times and said he would surrender after making a phone call, but repeatedly went back inside. During his final retreat into the home, deputies heard what appeared to be a gunshot. Knowing a woman and children were still inside and could be in danger, deputies entered the residence and evacuated them through a side window, the sheriffs office said. Deputies later found the man dead from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound. Authorities said there is no ongoing threat to the community. Detectives, crime scene technicians and investigators from the Medical Examiners Office are expected to remain at the scene for several hours as the investigation continues.

entry.title: Miami native and baseball Hall of Famer Andre Dawson receives the Governors Medal of Freedom
entry.summary: Baseball Hall of Famer Andre Dawson received the Governors Medal of Freedom. Governor Ron DeSantis said the award recognizes Dawsons baseball career, his contributions to Florida AM University, and his lasting impact on the state of Florida. Dawson was born in Miami and went to Southwest Miami Senior High School. He then went to Florida AM and walked on to the Rattlers baseball team. His performance led the Montreal Expos to select him in the 1975 MLB draft. His distinguished career in Major League Baseball, his contributions to the sport, and his lasting impact on our state have earned him this award. The Hawk has represented Florida in the best possible way for decades. His generous support of FAMU and its baseball program has helped generations of student-athletes succeed. The Governors Medal of Freedom is the highest honor I can bestow on any Floridian, and Andre Dawson truly deserves this recognition, DeSantis said. Past recipients of the Governors Medal of Freedom include Florida State University football coach Bobby Bowden, golfer Barbara Nicklaus, musician Jimmy Buffett, Coach Lee Corso, and former Florida Supreme Court Justice Charles Canady.
